description: I have many years of experience watching dogs for friends, neighbors and clients while they are out of town. I treat our furry guests as family. They are welcome to lounge around, snuggle up and play.  I just said goodbye to my best friend of 15 years. It was devastating, but it brings me peace knowing he is happy over the rainbow bridge. I look forward to cuddles with your fur baby.  I am a SAHM, so I am available to let your dog out for potty breaks multiple times a day and they will always be supervised when outside.  I have a fenced in backyard and I have baby gates around the house to separate the dog from the children if needed. I have doggy steps to assist climbing up onto the couch if they want to chill there.

I love animals and making sure they are happy, Always send photos and messages to keep the owner updated. I allow them to have lots of space in my house.  We have big and nice backyard and dogs can play any enjoys.  I'm house wife and my schedule is fixable.  I'm House wife and my schedule is fixable for weekdays or weekends.  I can provide the Pickup and drop off service for little extra charge.  I have a big fenced and safe nice backyard, Dogs always lots of space can walk / run and play. Water and Snakes and toys available.

We only host one dog at a time, so your pup will get our full attention, care, and love, just like family! It’s a calm, safe environment with no other pets around, except our own small Havanese, who’s very friendly and gentle.     I've been raising dogs since childhood, learning responsibility and love through each companion. Our current dog brings endless joy, loyalty, and deep connection to our family.  Your dog will be an integral part of our family, with constant companionship and love. As a stay-at-home mom, your dog will never be alone, always enjoying time with your friendly dog and having access to a spacious garden. Regular walks will ensure they stay happy and active.  We have a spacious garden where your dog can play, explore, and enjoy the outdoors. Our very friendly dog will be a great companion, offering constant companionship and gentle interactions. Together, they’ll have plenty of room for fun, exercise, and socializing, ensuring your dog feels right at home.

Hi there!   The pups’ happy eyes say it all — go take a look at our photos! 🐾  Check out our photo gallery!   I’m a professional dog sitter with years of hands-on experience and a heart full of love for animals. About three years ago, my family and I moved here from Europe, and since then, I’ve been offering personalized, high-quality care for pups of all breeds, sizes, and personalities.    I have a background in biology, canine behavior, and medical care, which helps me understand and support each dog’s unique needs. Whether your pup has a detailed medication schedule, special care instructions, or just needs a little extra TLC—I’ve got it covered.    Over the years, we’ve welcomed more than 200 furry friends into our lives. We treat every dog like family, and our home is always open for wagging tails and happy paws. Please check out the photos in my profile to meet some of our past guests!    We’d be thrilled to welcome your pup into our pack!    We think we teach animals, but on the contrary, animals teach us!     I had a dog, but unfortunately she passed away. Having a senior dog with health problems and joint problems I know how hard it is to leave a pet behind. I know how stressful it can be.  Your dog will be treated like family from the moment they arrive. I offer a safe, clean, and calm environment where your pup can feel relaxed and happy. We stick to your dog’s normal routine as much as possible—including feeding times, medication, walks, and play. I send regular updates, photos, and videos, so you can always feel close to your furry friend, even when you’re away.  1.I can take care of animals both at home and come to the client's house.  2.I create very comfortable conditions for animals.  Animals are happy to be with us.

Hello, I’m Josie! I love and adore dogs and have been caring for them for over 35 years. I would love to care for your furry family member in my home. I am a retired nurse with a sweet and friendly 10 lb Chihuahua-Yorkie mix named Yumi! I am usually always home all day so I can give your fur baby my full attention and all the care and playtime they need! I have a backyard and plentiful dog toys for them to enjoy to their heart’s content. I also love walking with them along the many gorgeous trails Coto has to offer! Feel free to message me for any questions 😊  I am retired and a homebody so I’ll be able to accommodate all your pup’s needs throughout the day. I have a backyard they can enjoy at their leisure and pee pads if they’re trained to go inside. They are welcome on my bed and sofas as I would allow for my own fur baby.  I have a fenced backyard they can enjoy, plus unlimited indoor playtime at home! Meal times and food type will be done to your specifications. I’ll be sure to follow your routines so they are most comfortable.

Lifelong pet owner and former vet tech with the Humane Society. I work from home, providing full-time care, including puppy training through to senior dog support. I'm excited to bring my established pet care experience to Laguna Hills!  Since I work from home full-time, your fur baby will enjoy attentive supervision, companionship, and a flexible routine tailored to their individual needs. Mornings begin with a potty break in our fully fenced backyard, followed by breakfast and supervised playtime or a relaxing walk, depending on your dog's energy level and preferences. Throughout the day, your dog can relax comfortably nearby while I work, enjoy frequent potty breaks, explore the backyard, and receive plenty of affection and attention. We typically head outside every couple of hours, with additional breaks whenever needed. Our friendly Bernedoodle, Mayzie, enjoys having compatible furry friends around, while Tommie, our senior Yorkshire Terrier, appreciates a more relaxed pace. I carefully supervise interactions and respect each dog's individual comfort level. Evenings include dinner, outdoor time, and a relaxed wind-down with plenty of opportunities for cuddles before bedtime. I follow your dog's established feeding, medication, exercise, and sleeping routines as closely as possible to help them feel comfortable and secure. With only one client household booked at a time, I can provide the personalized attention, consistency, and loving environment your fur baby deserves. And of course, you'll receive regular photo and video updates throughout their stay!  Safety and comfort come first in our home. We have a fully fenced yard for secure play, a flexible potty and play schedule.  Pets are never left alone for long, and we create a calm, supervised environment where they can feel safe, loved, and part of the family.

My husband and I love animals, we have over 30 years experience with pets of all kinds.  We have senior dogs and a 3 year old dog, Rafa and cats, we watch puppies as well.  Feed them as scheduled and medicines aren't a problem.  We also have a deaf dog we watch regularly.    I work full time, my hubby is self employed, home most of the day and we're always home on the weekends.  We get our pets groomed monthly and they get walks and we play with our pets.  They lay on the couch with us and sleep in our numerous pet beds or our bed.  We have a big fenced in yard that they can cruise around in and we stay with them outside at all times, especially smaller dogs.    I have 4 sweet dogs, with a big fenced in yard, three cats, two senior and one under 3, with a big fenced in Catio.  We are non smokers.  We have plenty of beds and toys for pets.  When we wake up in the morning, first thing is we let our dogs out, our Epileptic dog gets her meds, then we feed our cats first, then dogs.  We brush our dogs daily or every other day, depends on life and how busy we are.  We clean our yard every day, and do deep cleans on the weekends.  Our dog beds are washed weekly, and our dog bowls, which we have plenty and every size are washed every day.  We have small, medium and extra large water bowls all over the home and those are cleaned and refreshed daily.  We have a very large backyard that is secure and fenced.  We let dogs in the yard and one of us is always with them at all times and cleaned daily.

I love dogs . Since I was a child I have grown up with pets... I would love the opportunity to care for you pet . I prefer dogs who are potty trained, and for male dogs that don’t urinate or “mark” in my home by peeing everywhere , but will work with your dogs and care for them as my own.    Also PLEASE NO DROP OFFS before 7:00 am and  NO PICKUPS after 9:30 pm, otherwise, that would require another day's booking. No normal KENNEL or doggy daycare operates 24/7. I’m not a hotel open 24/7. I also do need to sleep and have other obligations . If you have an early morning flight or late night flight, please  accommodate accordingly between my hours of operation :7:00 am to 9:30 pm.  Please be respectful of peoples times and schedules. I am sure you wouldn’t want people coming to your door at 11pm or midnight to get their pet.  What you will get from me you won’t get at a commercial doggy daycare is that I don’t watch a ton of dogs! Usually 1-2 dogs MAX at a time. That way your pup is getting personalized attention. I only do this because this is not my main business and enjoy watching a few pets at a time because I like having dogs around me since my lovely Jack Russell died a few years back of old age and I miss having a pet around.  I work from home most days so can watch your dog and give the necessary supervision your pet needs!   Thanks and look forward to your reply! I look forward to watching your fur baby!  Work remote from home most time during weekdays  so can accommodate watching your pet during the day and evenings . Will be around your pet often.  Fenced area secured gate- dogs can’t escape plus I keep dogs inside my home and near me so they will be very safe with me.

I’m a foster for rescues. I have 45 years of experience and very reliable. I’ve had dogs all my life!  Life only gets better with a pet..  I have trained many dogs. I’ve house trained them, taught them to walk on a leash and taught them not to leave my yard (even when dogs/people walk by). In my opinion a house isn’t a home without a four legged best friend. I guarantee to treat your pet as one of own just like family. I have a big heart with a lot of love to give!!  I wake up every morning around 5:30 a.m. to start my day. I go for a walk and do things around the house. I prep dinner and run errands as needed.  In our home pets are treated as family!  They sleep in bed with us, go for car rides and frequent potty breaks/walks. We do have a small yard with a half a stucco wall. We make sure pets are never outside by themselves.

I have taken care of multiple dogs, ranging from very small to very large, for most of my life. I’ve dealt with the affection and attention required for a German Shepherd/ Malinois to the very relaxed nature of my chihuahua/miniature poodle.  My dog Bella requires frequent breaks to go outside and semi-frequent play. She gets plenty of play daily and is given affection and love whenever she needs it.  Any pet in my home will have a bed to lay on. They would be given attention and love and will have time to go on walks and play if required. I am a remote student and someone else in the house works from home so your pet will never be left alone.

Hello, I’m Muskaan, an 18-year-old responsible and passionate dog caregiver. I have a large backyard, enjoy long walks, and live near several dog parks—perfect for active pups. I’m experienced in administering medications and committed to providing safe, loving care. I’m also a licensed driver, making drop-offs or pet transport easy. I work part-time as a swim coach with young children and volunteer at my local hospital, which has strengthened my patience, empathy, and attention to detail. Your dog will be in caring, capable hands with me. I’d love the opportunity to care for your furry family member like my own!  I currently work part time- Tuesday and Saturday mornings, and Wednesday afternoons. Only working part time gives me plenty of time to dote on, care, love, and play with your furry friends.  I have a big fenced heard with plenty of room to run around and play. I have two parks walkable distance from my house so that your pups can let off any extra energy they have. There will always be someone at home in my house so your dog will never be left unattended. I have a family of 6 dogs lovers that would care endlessly for your dog with me.

I’ve taken care of dogs of different breeds and sizes for many years. Friends, family, and neighbors rely on me to walk, feed, and bathe their pets. I have experience with puppies, senior dogs, and pets. I treat every animal like my own and ensure they feel safe, loved, and happy.  I have full availability to care for your pets! I’m home all day and can provide constant attention, playtime, and care. I’m available for boarding, drop-ins, and walks throughout the week and on weekends.  In my home, pets are treated like family. I have a fenced yard, two friendly dogs, and two loving sons (ages 7 and 14) who grew up with pets and adore animals. Your dog will get lots of attention, playtime, and care in a clean, safe, and happy environment. I always follow your feeding, medication, and crate instructions to make sure your pet feels comfortable and loved.

I’m a stay-at-home mom with a lifelong love for animals and years of hands-on experience caring for dogs. My husband and I lead a healthy, active lifestyle—and our dogs are a big part of that! I go on walks with them three times a day, rain or shine, and make sure they stay happy, engaged, and well exercised.    Over the years, I’ve had the joy of sharing my life with two miniature Schnauzers and a Doberman Pinscher, all of whom have crossed the rainbow bridge. A few years later, I adopted another Doberman at just two months old and began training her to be a psychiatric service dog. She passed all her service dog tests by the age of six months and has been nothing short of phenomenal—gentle with kids, respectful around small dogs, and always ready to help.    Her best friend is our current miniature Schnauzer, and together they bring so much energy and love to our home. Our dogs are well-groomed, well-mannered, and treated like family—and yours will be too. We have a double-fenced backyard for safe outdoor play, and our home is always kept clean, calm, and welcoming.    I’m attentive to every detail: I give only bottled water, refreshed throughout the day, and I pride myself on providing a loving, safe environment. Every pup is unique, and I’ll make sure your dog’s individual needs are met so they feel comfortable, cared for, and right at home.    We’d love the chance to Meet & Greet your family and provide your pup with their own happy, tail-wagging vacation!  I’m home full-time and go on walks with the dogs three times a day. I wipe their paws and bodies after every walk. I keep my home clean and my dogs well-groomed, because their health and comfort matter to me. I give them only bottled water and refresh it several times a day to make sure they’re always hydrated with clean, fresh water. I care for every dog as if they were my own—with love, attention, and the highest standards. Every pup is happy and content after its own vacation staying with us.  We have a double-fenced backyard that offers a safe and secure space for dogs to play and explore. Our two friendly dogs are always happy to keep your pup company! However, I completely understand that every dog is different—if your pup prefers solo time or needs a quieter environment, we have plenty of space and flexibility to accommodate that. All dogs are welcome to sleep on the couch and human bed with us! Your dog’s comfort and happiness always come first.

😃 Hey pet parents!  Whether you need a doggie-free weekday or a vacation getaway, I understand. It’s important to know your pup is with someone trustworthy, caring and provides daily updates. I wouldn’t expect anything less for my own fur baby. Hi, I’m Annie! Every pup under my care will be loved and treated like family. ❤️  Please take a moment to look over my care style and policies to see if they align with what you and your pup is looking for before booking.     🐶 Care & Experience  	•	Over 20 years of hands-on dog care experience  	•	Maximum limit of 4 pups per night for personalized attention  	•	Hands on Dog and Cat CPR & First Aid Certified   	•	Patient, affectionate, and highly attentive caregiver    	•	Experienced with dogs of all ages, including seniors and special-needs pups  	•	Care customized to each dog’s routine, preferences, and needs  	•	Services offered: daycare, boarding, and drop-in visits  	•	My husband and I both work from home, so your pup will always have company. We bring dogs with us when we both need to go out and don’t leave them home alone. So far, we haven’t had to leave a dog alone. If we ever do, it would only be for an emergency.    💕 Daily Care & Updates  	•	Scheduled potty breaks every 2–3 hours  	•	Meals followed as instructed  	•	Plenty of cuddles, attention & enrichment  	•	Indoor and outdoor playtime  	•	Quality photos + updates sent daily    🌳 Exercise & Play  	•	Fenced side & backyard areas for safe play time with owners permission & weather permitting  	•	Park walk (with owners permission, weather permitting and my availability)   	•	Fun indoor / outdoor  play sessions to keep your pet engaged and happy throughout the day.    🏡 Home Environment  	•	Interior of home is calm, clean, and pet-friendly    	•	Single-family home with fenced outdoor areas          •	Property features well-kept grassy front and back yards, maintained weekly by a professional gardener  	•	During the rainy season or extreme  heat waves a canopy will be available to keep the doggies dry or cool for when they go potty in the backyard    🧼 Cleanliness & Safety  	•	Clean, pet-friendly home: thoroughly maintained weekly with mopping, vacuuming, and dusting  	•	 Freshly laundered pet bedding is provided after each guest arrival.  	•	We are a shoes off home. Fur guests coming indoors are wiped down with pet friendly wipes after outdoor time   	•	Flea prevention and vaccinations required for all guests  	•	Indoor & outdoor home security system  	•	Secure two-layer front door for added safety    💊 Medical & Special Care  	•	American Red Cross Cat & Dog First Aid Trained - 9/25/2025  	•	Pet Tech CPR & First Aid Certification Trained - 1/2026  	•	Experienced administering oral meds, eye drops, ear drops, topical meds, and insulin injections    *Medication Care is a special request add on service, add this service when booking. Please go over your pets medical and prescription needs at our meet and greet 😊     Medication Care - Add On Service:   	•	Oral / Topical medications: $8-$50 per day (depending on doses and frequency )  	•	Insulin injections: $15 per day Service:   	•	Round the clock care after ER: $100-$150 per day    🚕 Convenience - Add On Service   	•	Pick-up & drop-off available (one-way or round-trip)  available for day care, boarding, groomer, vet appointments     ⏰ Daycare & Boarding Hours ( Please Read Carefully)  	•	Daycare: Up to 8 hours per day (available hours to choose from: 8AM – 6PM)  	•	If you need daycare for more than 8 hours, please select the boarding option instead, as it offers more flexible hours  	•	Boarding: 24-hour period  	•	Drop-off time is your pick-up time  	•	1-hour grace period for pick-up; if additional time is need, please add extended care to your booking request     ✨ Please Read Before Booking! ✨  If additional time may be needed at pick-up, please be sure to add extended-care hours when making your booking. Rover does not automatically adjust for additional pick-up time, so this will need to be added manually. This helps ensure everything goes smoothly at pick-up, with no surprises. 🐶💛 Daycare includes up to 8 hours of care. Anytime over 9 hours please select boarding rates! Thank you! 😊     🐶 Meet & Greet: A required step before your first reservation with me. I want to make sure we are a good fit! Best of all, all meet and greets are FREE! I would love to meet your pet so let’s set one up!     During our meet-and-greet, I’ll gather details to create a personalized profile for your dog, including their daily routine, preferences, and any special needs. I’ll rely on these notes to make sure your pup feels comfortable and well cared for when they are with me.    If you decide to book, I’ll just ask for your dog’s most recent vaccination records and flea prevention info. This helps ensure all pups under my care are up to date. I’ll also provide a standard pet care waiver. This is a simple, common form used by all boarding and pet care providers.     ✨ Reservations   Each stay is carefully planned to ensure a comfortable and stress-free experience for you and your pup(s). Please refer to Rover’s cancellation policy for non-holiday and holiday stays if needed.     🎒 What to Bring for a Cozy & Happy Stay    To help your pup feel completely at home, we recommend bringing a few familiar comforts:    • Food (please provide pre-portioned meals if your pup has specific feeding preferences)  • Favorite treats  • Leash, collar, or harness  • Crate (if preferred for sleeping or comfort)  • A familiar blanket or bed with your scent  • Brush or grooming essentials  • Pee pads (if needed)• Diapers (if needed)    ✨ What’s Included During Their Stay    Your pup’s comfort and happiness are our top priorities. Every stay includes:    • Fresh food & water bowls  • Cozy dog bed  • Treats (please let us know about any allergies or dietary restrictions)  • Toys   • Pup wipes  • Poop bags    Together, these comforts create a warm and reassuring environment where your pup can feel safe, relaxed, and truly at home. 🐶  As a full-time Rover service provider, You’ll receive daily update with photos. Daily update are usually sent out in the evening time between 4-7pm so you never miss a moment of your pup’s day. 😊    Our routine:  For all the pups we start each mornings with potty break around 7:30am followed by breakfast unless other wise requested. Throughout the day, dogs are supervised and let out into the backyard every 3 hours for potty breaks. We love providing lots of love and attention through backyard playtime, calm indoor and outdoor activities, head scratches, and belly rubs. Mealtimes are always kept consistent with your dog’s regular routine.     I’m home most of the day and only step out occasionally for Rover walks, drop-in visits, or quick errands. During those times, dogs at home are supervised by my husband. Evenings are all about winding down with dinner, final potty breaks before settling in comfortably for the night.    Group Size & Temperaments  It’s always nice to make new friends! I keep boarding and daycare groups small, usually four to five dogs or fewer at a time. Each group is thoughtfully booked based on size, energy level, and personality to provided a positive experience for everyone. It’s a wonderful way for your pup to meet new friends in a calm, supervised environment.    Just a gentle reminder that space is limited and our availability tends to fill up quickly. We recommend booking early to secure your spot. We’d love to have your pup with us. Thank you for your understanding 😊🩷🐶  🛡️ Safety First    Your pup’s safety is my top priority. I ’m trained in American Red Cross Cat & Dog First Aid. I’ve also completed my hands on trading and received my Pet Tech CPR & First Aid Certification, 2026     All walks are always leashed, we avoid interactions with other dogs, and our home is fully secured with locked gates, a two-layer front door, and in/outdoor security. Backyard play, sun bathing and potty breaks are always supervised.

I've been on Rover as a pet owner for the last 12 years, until my sweet dog recently passed, so I know exactly what I was looking for in a pet sitter: Present, dependable and watched after my dog as their own.     I grew up in a home always full of cats and dogs, so caring for animals has never felt like a job to me, it's just how I live. As an adult with my wife, Karolina and I shared our home with my precious cat, Sam, that I brought into our relationship who I raised from kittenhood and through his final senior years. Our first furbaby we had together was Huxley, our larger than life, large breed Samoyed who was truly like a child to us, until he passed away very recently. Sam and Huxley got along so well.     Having a large breed dog and cats living together taught me a lot about reading different animals' needs and keeping the peace in a multi-pet household. I'm comfortable with all breeds, but we have a real soft spot for large dogs, since that's where most of my hands-on experience lies. I am also experienced giving medication and managing special diets, so pets with health needs are in good hands with me.     My dogs were always well trained and well cared for. Because Huxley was reactive around some dogs, Karolina and I became very attentive to reading body language and managing introductions to other animals carefully. I know how to keep every pet in my care feeling safe and comfortable, whether they're social butterflies or a little more cautious. I also keep a close eye on behavioral changes, so if anything seems off, I catch it early.    After recently losing our sweet boys, Huxley, and Sam a few years before, I would be heartened to fill our home with the joy of your fur baby.  My wife, Karolina, and I will be devoted to your pet. We're self-employed and both work from home, so we have flexible schedules built around pets, not the other way around. We can take time throughout the day for potty breaks, walks, feeding, playtime, or just some extra cuddle time. I loved taking my own dog on long daily walks, and we'd often head out for bigger adventures too, like the beach or harbor, local hikes, parks, outdoor malls, wherever he wanted to explore. Or even just a pet friendly restaurant experience. Your pet won't be an afterthought squeezed into our day. They'll be part of it.  Our home is a two-story house with a small, secure fenced yard, and the neighborhood has great walking routes and green common areas, perfect for both quick bathroom breaks and longer walks. Inside, we have a large crate if needed (Huxley just slept in it with the door open), dog beds, water bowls throughout the house and a stash of toys ready to go, so your pet has familiar comforts and a safe space to settle into from day one.     There are no other pets or kids living in the home, so your pet will get my full attention.     I'm experienced with medication schedules and special diets, and I take introductions and routines seriously to help pets feel settled and comfortable quickly. Whether it's a young, energetic dog or an older pet who needs a little extra care, I'll treat them like they're my own and with no less love than we gave Huxley, which was an embarrassingly great amount of love.

My husband and I are an active couple with 2 young kids, I am a stay at home mom and Johnny works for the fire department. The kids and I are always outside exploring/taking walks. When Johnny is home, he is very active and looking for dogs to take trail running! Johnny and I both love dogs and grew up with them in our homes, having breeds from Dobermans to Chihuahuas. My kids love dogs as well and are so excited to welcome them into our home!   We live in a 3 story townhouse right in front of a walking & bike trail, we have a fenced in front patio but no grass, so there will be lots of walks.  We have been the go-to dog sitters for friends and family & now want to open our home to our neighbors & their pups. We provide lots of treats, photos, cuddles, walks & many hours of outdoor time! Please feel free to ask any questions regarding our home & experience. :)  I am a stay at home mom so your pup will fit right in! We don’t leave for long periods of time (trip to store or gym, etc) so your pup will always be in good company.  Our patio is fenced in & safe. We will respect all rules you require for your dog! We accommodate special rules & diets. We want your dog to feel at home here.

I'm a Certified Positive Reinforcement Dog Trainer, working part-time with two dog training organizations as a Trainer and Behavior Specialist.  I've had the pleasure of working with dogs of all ages, from playful puppies to wise adults. Through my certifications and experience, I've developed a keen understanding of dog body language, behaviors, and their significance.  My expertise includes puppy training, obedience, impulse control, leash walking, managing leash reactivity, and regulating prey drive. Additionally, I love teaching fun and useful tricks using positive reinforcement techniques. In my sessions, I utilize a combination of rewards and praise to ensure a positive experience for your furry babies.  I’ve recently updated my work's schedule to better serve my furry clients and their families! I am available for full-day care and training every weekend, Tuesday, and Thursday, with additional early morning and evening sessions available on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays.  ✨✨✨Overview of Services - PLEASE READ ✨✨✨  🏠FOR BOARDING SERVICES🏠: Recently, I lost my beloved companion to bone cancer after an eight-month battle. He was my soul dog, and his absence is deeply felt. Currently, my home doesn't have any pets, but it's perfectly suited for dogs of all sizes. I prefer to host only one dog at a time, ensuring they receive undivided attention, ample playtime, and the affection they deserve.  💛Note: If your dog has separation anxiety, please let me know in advance. This allows me to coordinate with my partner's schedule to ensure 100% coverage during my working hours.  ✨ Premium Add-Ons  Focused Training Session | $30 | 30 minutes  Nature Trail Hike | $20 | 1-2hours  Beach Exploration | $20 | 1-2 hours  🐕‍🦺FOR DOG-WALKING SERVICES🐕‍🦺: I believe walks should be stress-free experiences for our furry companions. To achieve this, I emphasize the proper use of tools and techniques. For dogs prone to pulling, I advocate for anti-pull tools like front-clip harnesses or head halters. For those who walk politely, back-clip harnesses are suitable. Additionally, I prioritize mental stimulation and allow ample time for sniffing and exploration to keep your pup happy and fulfilled during our walks.  💛Leash-Reactive Dogs - If your furry companion is leash-reactive, please inform me in advance so we can make the necessary preparations and set them up for success during our walks. Your dog's comfort and safety are paramount, and by knowing their specific needs, I can tailor our outings to ensure a positive and enjoyable experience for both of us.   **I do not accept dogs who wear any aversive tools. Instead, I focus on positive reinforcement techniques and gentle methods to encourage good behavior and a pleasant walking experience.**  🚶FOR DROP-IN SERVICES🚶: I can feed your pet, take them out for a potty break, and even go for a quick walk around the block. Please provide clear feeding instructions or any necessary medical instructions beforehand to ensure your pet's needs are met with the utmost care and attention.

Dogs have been part of my life for as long as I can remember. I grew up with German Shepherds, a Cocker Spaniel, and a mixed-breed dog. Later, when I started my own family, we welcomed Fiera, our Labrador Retriever. She grew up alongside my children—they were like siblings and partners in crime. If you’ve ever had a Lab, you know exactly what I mean. 😁 When Fiera was about five years old, Glitch, our little Shihpoo, joined the family. Fiera crossed the Rainbow Bridge at 13, and we still miss her every day. 💗 Making your pup feel safe and cared for is my priority. If your dog isn’t acting like themselves, isn’t eating normally, or just seems “off,” I’ll notice and I’ll let you know.  I’m comfortable following detailed instructions, whether it’s feeding routines, walks, medications, or special care. I have experience giving oral medications, eye and ear medications, topical treatments, and subcutaneous injections when prescribed by a veterinarian. When I’m caring for your dog, I’ll keep you updated with photos and messages.  While you’re away, I’m also happy to bring in mail and packages, water indoor or outdoor plants, rotate lights if requested, and help keep your home looking lived-in. IMPORTANT, please read:   Who is the 1%:   👹 This is *NOT* for dogs with problematic, aggressive, reactive, or dangerous behavior. I am not currently offering my dog training services. I do not work with retractable leashes.   🚽 Absolutely no accidents indoors.   🤝 Meet and greet required.   —   A hunting dog attacked me when I was four years old. On my way to the cul-de-sac mailbox, it jumped the fence and slammed my head onto the concrete. Scalp split open, I ran home screaming. From then on, dogs terrified me. I hid behind my mum around dogs bigger than me…and at the time, every dog was. I declared myself a cat person, and that was that.   Then YouTube appeared. The algorithm’s “infinite wisdom” served up a video of Cesar Millan transforming a “mean” dog into a “nice” one in five minutes. Were all dogs really this easy to understand? If I could do what Cesar did, if I could master dog training, maybe they wouldn't scare me anymore? It became an obsession. I watched thousands of his videos. Before/after. Wild/controlled. Chaos/manageable. Scary/incredibly cute.   But watching dogs on a screen was a different beast than working with them in real life. My great aunt in Cape Town, South Africa, gave me my first round of exposure therapy when she took me to a Great Dane farm. Dozens of giant dogs loomed around me. She held my hand the whole time and introduced me to every. single. one. I can do this. I can do this.   She has since passed, but being around dogs reconnects me to her memory. It's a heartwarming comfort.   Years later, a friend was having trouble on her walk. “Can I try?” I gave her a few concrete instructions from my musings:   “Krishna, you’re really good with dogs. She never listens to anyone else, but she’s perfectly calm with you.” “What? Nahhh, she can just sense I’m vegan.”    I assumed everyone understood dog body language and I was just slow on the uptake. Turns out, they don't! Not only was I no longer afraid, I was giving lessons!   Today, clients fly me across the globe to care for their dogs. My last assignment took me to London for two glorious, busy weeks.   While I hope to have a dog of my own again someday, I want to dedicate my time to caring for yours in the meantime.   If you’re looking for training tips, check out Hamilton Dog Training on YouTube. His methods are incredible.   I look forward to meeting your lil best friend!  I grew up between Kansas and England. So you might notice some funny spellings on my page. I hid behind my mum around dogs bigger than me…and at the time, every dog was. I declared myself a cat person, and that was that.   Then YouTube appeared. The algorithm’s “infinite wisdom” served up a video of Cesar Millan transforming a “mean” dog into a “nice” one in five minutes. Were all dogs really this easy to understand? If I could do what Cesar did, if I could master dog training, maybe they wouldn't scare me anymore? It became an obsession. I watched thousands of his videos. Before/after. Wild/controlled. Chaos/manageable. Scary/incredibly cute.   But watching dogs on a screen was a different beast than working with them in real life. My great aunt in Cape Town, South Africa, gave me my first round of exposure therapy when she took me to a Great Dane farm. Dozens of giant dogs loomed around me. She held my hand the whole time and introduced me to every. single. one. I can do this. I can do this.   She has since passed, but being around dogs reconnects me to her memory. On my way to the cul-de-sac mailbox, it jumped the fence and slammed my head onto the concrete. Scalp split open, I ran home screaming. From then on, dogs terrified me. I hid behind my mum around dogs bigger than me…and at the time, every dog was. I declared myself a cat person, and that was that.   Then YouTube appeared. The algorithm’s “infinite wisdom” served up a video of Cesar Millan transforming a “mean” dog into a “nice” one in five minutes. Were all dogs really this easy to understand? If I could do what Cesar did, if I could master dog training, maybe they wouldn't scare me anymore? It became an obsession. I watched thousands of his videos. Before/after. Wild/controlled. Chaos/manageable. Scary/incredibly cute.   But watching dogs on a screen was a different beast than working with them in real life. My great aunt in Cape Town, South Africa, gave me my first round of exposure therapy when she took me to a Great Dane farm. Dozens of giant dogs loomed around me. She held my hand the whole time and introduced me to every. single. one. I can do this. I can do this.   She has since passed, but being around dogs reconnects me to her memory. It's a heartwarming comfort.   Years later, a friend was having trouble on her walk. “Can I try?” I gave her a few concrete instructions from my musings:   “Krishna, you’re really good with dogs. She never listens to anyone else, but she’s perfectly calm with you.” “What? Nahhh, she can just sense I’m vegan.”    I assumed everyone understood dog body language and I was just slow on the uptake. Turns out, they don't! Not only was I no longer afraid, I was giving lessons!   Today, clients fly me across the globe to care for their dogs. My last assignment took me to London for two glorious, busy weeks.   While I hope to have a dog of my own again someday, I want to dedicate my time to caring for yours in the meantime.   If you’re looking for training tips, check out Hamilton Dog Training on YouTube. His methods are incredible.   I look forward to meeting your lil best friend!  I grew up between Kansas and England. So you might notice some funny spellings on my page. This is dog sitting for the 1% who have already taken their training seriously and want a loving substitute while you're gone. IMPORTANT, please read:   Who is the 1%:   👹 This is *NOT* for dogs with problematic, aggressive, reactive, or dangerous behavior. I am not currently offering my dog training services. I own a lot of precious items; my neighbours are in close quarters and we all work together to keep a quiet environment. Barking excessively or at random 3am noises is not acceptable.   👵 For larger dogs, I have elderly neighbours that I interact with daily. Jumping up on people is not safe for them or tolerated.   🏆 Your dog understands loose-leash walking. I do not work with retractable leashes.   🚽 Absolutely no accidents indoors.   🤝 Meet and greet required.   —   A hunting dog attacked me when I was four years old. On my way to the cul-de-sac mailbox, it jumped the fence and slammed my head onto the concrete. Scalp split open, I ran home screaming. From then on, dogs terrified me. I hid behind my mum around dogs bigger than me…and at the time, every dog was. I declared myself a cat person, and that was that.   Then YouTube appeared. The algorithm’s “infinite wisdom” served up a video of Cesar Millan transforming a “mean” dog into a “nice” one in five minutes. Were all dogs really this easy to understand? If I could do what Cesar did, if I could master dog training, maybe they wouldn't scare me anymore? It became an obsession. I watched thousands of his videos. Before/after. Wild/controlled. Chaos/manageable. Scary/incredibly cute.   But watching dogs on a screen was a different beast than working with them in real life. My great aunt in Cape Town, South Africa, gave me my first round of exposure therapy when she took me to a Great Dane farm. Dozens of giant dogs loomed around me. She held my hand the whole time and introduced me to every. single. one. I can do this. I can do this.   She has since passed, but being around dogs reconnects me to her memory. It's a heartwarming comfort.   Years later, a friend was having trouble on her walk. “Can I try?” I gave her a few concrete instructions from my musings:   “Krishna, you’re really good with dogs. She never listens to anyone else, but she’s perfectly calm with you.” “What? Nahhh, she can just sense I’m vegan.”    I assumed everyone understood dog body language and I was just slow on the uptake. Turns out, they don't! Not only was I no longer afraid, I was giving lessons!   Today, clients fly me across the globe to care for their dogs. My last assignment took me to London for two glorious, busy weeks.   While I hope to have a dog of my own again someday, I want to dedicate my time to caring for yours in the meantime.   If you’re looking for training tips, check out Hamilton Dog Training on YouTube. His methods are incredible.   I look forward to meeting your lil best friend!  I grew up between Kansas and England. So you might notice some funny spellings on my page. A boarding day runs 24 hours from drop-off. Drop off at 8:30 a.m. and pick-up is 8:30 a.m. the next day. Late pick-ups are $20 per hour, per dog, and never cost more than one day's rate: at four hours past your time, it becomes another boarding day. A pick-up after 7:00 p.m. also counts as another day. If your travel plans shift, tell me as early as you can and I'll do what I can to work around them.  Safety comes first, and most of it happens before your dog ever arrives. We meet first, on neutral ground. Every stay starts with a meet-and-greet at the Yorba Linda Community Center, where dogs meet without anyone defending territory. It's also when I learn your dog's routine, quirks, and what makes them comfortable. Vaccinations are required. Proof of rabies, DHPP, and Bordetella protects your dog, the other dogs here, and everyone in the house. Introductions are slow. New dogs spend their first two to four hours in a separate section of the house. Dogs read the world through their noses, and that time lets everyone get used to a new scent before meeting. The first introduction then happens outside, on neutral ground. Meals are served apart. Every dog eats in a separate space. It takes a few extra minutes and removes the most common reason dogs scuffle in a group home. The house is dog-proofed. Food and anything harmful is stored out of reach, the trash bin is tall and commercial-grade, and I clean with pet-safe products. Paws get wiped with baby-safe sanitizing wipes before coming inside. The yard is fully fenced. Your dog has run of the house and the yard, always supervised. The kitchen and our bedroom stay off limits for hygiene, and gates make that easy. Between stays I walk the fence line looking for gaps and loose boards, keep toxic plants, tools, and lawn chemicals out of the yard, and make sure there's shade and fresh water whenever it's warm. Collars and harnesses get a fit check before we head out, and gates stay shut during drop-off and pick-up, which is when most escapes happen. Eyes on the house. A Ring camera system lets me check in if I step out briefly, and I have AirTags for dogs who are a flight risk. If something goes wrong. Before every stay I save your vet's details and confirm which emergency clinic nearest to us is open, so nobody is looking up an address at 2 a.m. I call you first and take your dog to your vet. If it's urgent and I can't reach you, we go straight to the emergency clinic and I keep calling until I reach you. Fireworks and holidays. The Fourth of July and New Year's Eve are the hardest nights of the year for dogs. Everyone is inside and secure well before dark, curtains closed, with music or the TV on to cover the noise, and nobody goes out without a leash and ID tags. If your dog panics at fireworks, tell me what helps and we'll plan around it. My home is clean, cozy, and set up around dogs rather than around a business. Photos of the house, the yard, and the trail are on my profile.
